decisions.reason: The accelerator program is featured visibly on the home page and signals the firm's announced circular-economy direction, so dropping it would publicly reverse a commitment, though it needs little investment and sits outside the firm's core machinery business.

The bio-based bitumen binder has its own page, ties into the firm's CO2-negative narrative and draws on development effort it would have to write off, and weak early results can still be blamed on a market that takes time to adopt such materials.
The infectious waste plant is a publicly announced partnership with ERMAFA promoted on the home page as revolutionary, so heavy invested and public commitment makes withdrawal very unlikely.
The mobile SNOWFLAKE plant is close to the core WASTX modular line, is highlighted as the latest product, and is central to the decentralized recycling strategy, so management would persist with it.
